Accus Offence Charged of Section 14 Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation )Act, 1986 Plea of Accused Not Guilty Date of commission of offence April to June 2016 Date of registration of FIR 16.07.2016 Date of filing of chargesheet 16.01.2017 Date of reserving order 25.01.2024 Date of Judgment 28.02.2024 Final Order ACQUITTAL Digitally s by NIDHI NIDHI SINGH SINGH Date: 2024.02.28 17:30:19 +0 State v Annu Aggarwal FIR No. 591/2016 PS NEB SARAI Page 1 of -:BRIEF FACTS AND REASONS FOR DECISION:- State vs Annu Aggarwal on 28 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76286395/ 1 1. In brief, the story of the prosecution is that on 27.06.2016, Ms. Pooja D/o Late Sh. Ram Gulam aged 14 years was reported to be missing and accordingly the FIR bearing no. 544/2016 was registered at PS Neb Sarai under Section 363 IPC. On 29.06.2016, Ms. Pooja was traced and produced before CWC where she stated that she was placed at work at Saket H-Block and her employer's name is Ms. Annu. She also stated that she used to take care of two children Rachit, aged 10 years and Lalit, aged 2 years, her work hours were 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM and worked for approximately 3 months. She stated that she worked for April, May and June and left her employment on 23.06.2024 and was paid Rs. 12,000/- for the entire period and was also provided food. She further stated before the SDM that during her employment, she had a peaceful time, she was not harassed in any manner, ,was provided food and was being kept with love and affection. 2. Upon completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed u/s 173 Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.P.C.') under Section 14 of Child and Adolescent Labour Act, 1986 was filed on 16.01.2017. Cognizance was taken on the same day and a copy of the charge sheet was supplied to the accused in compliance with Section 207 Cr.P.C on 03.04.2017. 3. After considering the record and hearing the arguments, charge u/s 14 of Child and Adolescent Labour( Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (hereinafter referred as Child Labour Act) was framed against the accused Annu Aggarwal on 16.05.2017 to which the accused pleaded "not guilty" and claimed trial. The matter then was listed for Prosecution Evidence (hereinafter referred to as, 'PE'). NIDHI Digitally signed by NIDHI SINGH SINGH Date: 2024.02.28 17:30:28 +0530 4. The accused admitted the genuineness of certain documents- the FIR 591/2016 (without contents, Ex. P-1) .Therefore formal examination of the corresponding witness was dispensed with under section 294 Cr.P.C and the above said document was directed to be read in evidence without their formal proof. 5. PW/ WCt. Mithilesh was dropped from PE upon request for the same by Ld. APP on 21.03.2018. Vide order dated 10.05.2019, it was observed that PW/ Pooja had expired on 13.08.2008. 6. During the trial, prosecution led the following oral and documentary evidence against the accused to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt-: Oral Evidence a. Pooja PW-1 b. Guddi (mother of Pooja) PW-2 c. Reeta Singh, Primary Teacher, SDMC Primary PW-3 Girls School-1, Devli, New Delhi d. ASI Rajender Singh PW-4 Documentary Evidence a. Complaint of Ms. Pooja Ex. PW1/A b. School Admission Form dated 18.07.2008 Ex . PW3/A c. Affidavit of father of Pooja Ex. PW3/B d. Date of birth certificate issued by MC Primary Ex. PW3/C Girls School e. School documents of Ms. Pooja Ex. Affidavit of brother of Pooja Ex. PW4/B g. Statement of Ms. Pooja recorded before SDM Ex. PW4/C h. Digitally signed NIDHI bySINGH NIDHI SINGH Date: 2024.02.28 17:30:59 +0530 19.
texts.facts: Upon directions of CWC, the present FIR bearing no. 591/2016 was registered at PS Neb Sarai against accused/ Annu Aggarwal. After examination of above cited witnesses, PE was closed vide order dated 17.12.2020. 8. To enable the accused to personally explain the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against him, the statement of the accused/ Annu Aggarwal, without oath, was recorded under Section 313 r/w 281 Cr.P.C on 02.04.2022. In reply, the accused asserted her innocence and stated that she had employed only the mother of victim Pooja ie Ms. Guddi and Ms. Guddi brought her daughter/Pooja along with her for her safety as there used to be no one at the residence of Guddi and she could not leave her daughter/ Pooja alone. Later, Pooja ran away with her boyfriend, and subsequently got married to him. She has stated that she has been falsely implicated in the present case. She chose to lead evidence in her defence. 9. Accused examined Mr. Arjun/ husband of Ms. Pooja in her defence. DW-1/ Mr. Arjun stated that he has known Ms. Pooja since 2015. At that time she was 14 years old. He got married to Pooja in 2019.
texts.arguments: Ld. APP submitted that the case has been proved beyond reasonable doubt with the testimonies of all PWs and documents relied upon during evidence and has thus prayed that the accused be convicted of the offence charged u/s 14 Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986. Ld. counsel finally submitted that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and that, therefore, the benefit of the same ought to be extended to the accused, and that the accused is liable to be acquitted of the alleged offence.

10. Short point for determination before this court is as under:
"Whether- Ms. Pooja was under 14 years of age in April of 2016?
And if she was, was she being employed as a domestic worker by Ms. Annu Aggarwal/ accused during the period April to June 2016?"

Digitally signed by NIDHI NIDHI SINGH SINGH Date:
2024.02.28 17:30:38 +0530 11.
This Court has given thoughtful consideration to the material appearing on record as well as the arguments.
Before dwelling into the facts of the present case, it would be apt to discuss the legal standards required to be met by both sides.
In criminal law, the burden of proving the guilt of the accused exclusively lies on the prosecution which must prove the offences charged beyond reasonable doubt.
The benefit of doubt, if any, must go in favour of the accused.
Digitally signed by NIDHI NIDHI SINGH SINGH

17. Coming to the testimonies of prosecution witnesses, PW-1/Ms. Pooja herself has stated in her evidence recorded on 28.06.2017 that she is 17/18 years of age.
The alleged employment at the house of the accused is stated to have been done in April 2016 which makes her 16 years of age at the time of her employment.
The husband of Ms. Pooja ie Mr. Arjun/DW-1 has been examined in Court who has admitted that she was 15 years of age in the year 2016 and that he got married to her in the year 2019.
Further, mother of Ms. Pooja ie PW-2/ Ms. Guddi has also stated in her evidence recorded on 21.03.2018 that "...Today my daughter is 18 years of age...".
She has further stated in her evidence that she used to take her daughter along with her to play with the children.
She has further stated in her cross examination that at the time of death of her husband in 2009, her daughter was 8-10 years of age and that her son Deepak was 10-12 years of age.
Her husband was illiterate but only knew how to append his signatures.

She has further stated that she had gotten her daughter Ms. Pooja admitted in school and at the time of admission in school, Pooja's age was 7 NIDHI Digitally signed by NIDHI SINGH SINGH Date: 2024.02.28 17:30:54 +0530 years and that affida
PW-4 has stated in his cross examination that Mr. Deepak, brother of Ms. Pooja, was 20 years old on 27.06.2016 and had lodged a missing complaint.
Prosecution has tried to establish the age of Ms. Pooja only through the school documents received from the concerned School.
No bone ossification test report is on record and there is no birth certificate also on record to prove the exact age of Ms. Pooja.

Further, PW-3/ Ms.
Reeta Singh, primary school teacher from SDMC Primary Girls School, Devli Village has reflected in her evidence that no birth documents such as birth certificate issued by MCD were seen at the time of admission in School.

Section 10 of the Child Labour Act states that if any question arises between an Inspector and an occupier as to the age of any child who is employed or is permitted to work by him in an establishment, the question shall, in the absence of
In the present case, IO has not taken due steps to confirm the age of the victim from a medical authority.

18. In criminal jurisprudence, an accused is presumed to be innocent, until proven guilty, and the burden of proving the guilt of the accused solely rests upon the prosecution by leading positive evidence.
Accused is not expected to prove his innocence to the hilt.

If the prosecution appears to be State vs Annu Aggarwal on 28 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76286395/
5 improbable or lacks credibility the benefit of doubt necessarily has to go to the accused.
The guilt of the accused is not to be proved by mere preponderance of probabilities but it has to be proved beyond all reasonable doubts.

It is for the prosecution to travel the entire distance from "may have"
to "must have".
Suspicion, howsoever grave, cannot take the place of proof.

Thus, in view of the foregoing analysis, this court is of the considered view that the aforesaid deficiencies in the case of the prosecution are sufficient to raise a doubt on the veracity of the entire prosecution case against the accused

Prosecution has miserably failed in proving its case beyond reasonable doubt that Ms. Pooja was firstly under 14 years of age in April 2016 and that she was employed by the accused as a domestic worker.
Accordingly, accused Annu Aggarwal stands acquitted of the offence under Section 14 of Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 in the present case.
Announced in open Court on this 29th day of February 2024.
